title: Deeper/broader PLOTSETTINGS RenderPreset graph and version boundary
mode: Autodesk primary-source research plus independent open-source implementation cross-check
question: What is documented about standalone PLOTSETTINGS RenderPreset references, and do open-source readers establish code-76/code-333 wire and consumer behavior?

sources.finding: Modern RapidRT presets live in ACAD_RENDER_RAPIDRT_SETTINGS; ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS stores a copy for assignment to a Viewport or PlotSettings.
Pre-2016 MentalRay presets use ACAD_RENDER_SETTINGS; ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS stores a copy for assignment to a Viewport or PlotSettings.
RenderPreset requires an ObjectId to a RenderSettings object.
The current API enum defines VisualStyle as 4 and RenderPreset as 5.
The current PLOTSETTINGS DXF table documents shade modes 0–3 and optional code 333, but does not document mode 5; this is an evidence gap for serialized wire and consumer acceptance.
RAPIDRTRENDERSETTINGS is a typed DXF object with handle and owner-dictionary links and positional fields.
MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS is a typed DXF object; the documentation notes the renderer is unavailable in later products while data is retained for backward compatibility.
LibreDWG lists the RapidRT and MentalRay object families separately.
LibreDWG marks these render-settings families unstable; its object-name mapping is only a family cross-check, not semantic evidence.
The current ACadSharp shade-mode enum enumerates values 0–3 only; this is implementation coverage evidence, not proof that higher AutoCAD API values are invalid.
ACadSharp maps PLOTSETTINGS code 76 to ShadePlotMode and code 333 to an ignored reference-valued handle property; the model does not document a rooted RenderSettings graph or mode-5 behavior.
ezdxf documents shade_plot_mode 0–3 and explicitly says it is unsure whether standalone PLOTSETTINGS objects occur; it cannot corroborate standalone mode 5.
LibreDWG's DWG object schema carries PLOTSETTINGS shadeplot_type at DXF group 76 and shadeplot handle at group 333; this establishes a field model, not the typed mode-5 target family.
LibreDWG's cross-reference matcher associates PLOTSETTINGS shadeplot code 333 with VISUALSTYLE. Treat as conservative implementation evidence, not proof RenderSettings targets are invalid.

An Autodesk Community post reports shade mode values 4 and 5 and code-333 associated targets, but it is user-authored and does not replace a producer-authored DXF witness or native save/reopen and plot check.

conclusion.documentedNamedCopyRoute: ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS stores a preset copy assignable to PlotSettings/Viewport
conclusion.openSourceMode5Corroboration: not found: ACadSharp and ezdxf document 0–3; LibreDWG maps shadeplot and its cross-reference matcher treats code 333 as VISUALSTYLE
conclusion.implementationDisposition: Keep only same-source-version DXF raw replay of a complete rooted typed/raw graph; treat it as local structural preservation only. Require release-specific native save/reopen plus actual plotted output before semantic support claims.

implementationReadiness: Require NOD[ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS] -> one complete NOD-owned dictionary -> one key/name-matched RapidRT or MentalRay typed/raw object; require PLOTSETTINGS code 333 to target that exact object.
Replay the raw positional RenderSettings groups at the identical source/target DXF version; use the existing object handle map for group 5, owner 330, and PlotSettings group 333.

Keep mode 0–3 null-only, mode 4 VISUALSTYLE-only, and reject wrong roots, duplicate roots/keys/handles, unpaired callbacks, mismatched owners, dangling targets, unsupported families, and version conversion.

Run generated in-memory ASCII/Binary controls for both RapidRT and MentalRay with collision, malformed-graph, sentinel-preservation, and same-adapter retry assertions; no checked-in drawing fixture and no new CTest registration.

Before release/version expansion, acquire one native-authored standalone PLOTSETTINGS mode-5 DXF witness for each renderer family; record code 76/333 order, owner/key graph, native reopen result, and plotted output.
Compare each qualified witness with targeted ACadSharp and LibreDWG runs; record acceptance and semantic loss rather than treating exit status as support evidence.
